name: Pudding public-story study corpus
purpose: Qualitative study of recurring editorial operations in selected public The Pudding stories. This is not training data, a style-cloning dataset, or an official Pudding rubric.

annotation_policy.copying: Store URLs, titles, coarse metadata, and original editorial annotations only. Do not copy article prose, visual assets, or proprietary styling.
annotation_policy.use: Study why a visual form earns its place, what cognitive job interaction performs, how evidence is gathered, and where reader agency enters.
annotation_policy.non_affiliation: pudding-skill is independent and is not affiliated with or endorsed by The Pudding.

stories.title: Film Dialogue by Gender
stories.question: Can an anecdotal debate about gender imbalance in films be measured at screenplay scale?
stories.argument_pattern: Turn a familiar cultural complaint into a census, then move from individual examples to population-level patterns and caveats.
stories.human_angle: Readers already recognize unequal representation; the project gives that lived observation a measurable frame without pretending the metric captures every dimension of a role.
stories.visual_necessity: Thousands of films and several cuts by gender, age, genre, and lead status are much easier to reason about through repeated visual comparisons than through prose or a table.
stories.design_move: Start with an accessible subset, expand to the full corpus, then let readers inspect films and categories.
stories.caveat_mode: Method limitations are tied directly to screenplay coverage, character thresholds, and script-to-screen differences.
stories.editorial_lesson: A strong visual essay can originate from doing the unglamorous data collection needed to move a cultural argument beyond rhetoric.
stories.anti_copy_note: Learn the census-to-example structure; do not imitate its visual styling or reuse its dataset without checking terms.

stories.title: Women's Pockets are Inferior
stories.question: How much less functional are pockets in women's jeans than comparable men's jeans?
stories.argument_pattern: Measure an everyday frustration directly, quantify the physical disparity, then translate dimensions into concrete object-fit consequences.
stories.human_angle: The premise begins with a mundane recurring annoyance that many readers physically experience, so the measurements answer a felt question rather than an abstract metric.
stories.visual_necessity: Pocket outlines, dimensions, and object-fit tests make physical constraints spatially legible in a way percentages alone cannot.
stories.design_move: Use a stable physical metaphor—the pocket itself—through the guided section, then let the reader test familiar objects.
stories.caveat_mode: Sample construction, waist-size matching, store collection, and geometric fit assumptions are exposed in methods.
stories.editorial_lesson: When no dataset exists for a culturally resonant irritation, collecting a small but carefully designed dataset can create both soul and a distinctive visual metaphor.
stories.anti_copy_note: Reuse the principle of measuring lived experience and designing around the object being measured, not the pocket silhouette treatment itself.

stories.title: The Structure of Stand-Up Comedy
stories.question: Why does the biggest laugh in a long stand-up routine work so well?
stories.argument_pattern: Begin at a memorable climax, work backward through local causes, then zoom out to reveal the structure that makes the moment land.
stories.human_angle: The reader is invited to re-experience a performance and discover craft hidden beneath something that initially feels spontaneous.
stories.visual_necessity: A routine's nested topics, callbacks, timing, and laughter duration are structural relationships; mapping them makes the argument visible rather than merely asserted.
stories.design_move: Use navigation and progressive decomposition so the same performance moves from line-level detail to thematic form and back again.
stories.caveat_mode: The project states that captions and topic boundaries were manually annotated and collectively reviewed.
stories.editorial_lesson: The best narrative operation may be reverse-engineering: start with the thing that made the author curious, then reveal the invisible structure beneath it.
stories.anti_copy_note: Learn the climax-to-structure reveal; do not replicate its specific performance assets or navigation choreography.

stories.title: The Words That Are ‘Most Hip Hop’
stories.question: Which words and artists are distinctive to hip hop when compared with a broader musical corpus?
stories.argument_pattern: Teach an increasingly sophisticated method through concrete examples, then let the reader use the resulting map as cultural exploration.
stories.human_angle: Technical language analysis is anchored in artists, slang, regions, and musical identity that readers may already care about.
stories.visual_necessity: Odds, term centrality, artist similarity, and high-dimensional neighborhoods become intelligible through spatial encodings and staged examples.
stories.design_move: Use one familiar word or artist to establish each analytical concept before exposing the full high-dimensional result.
stories.caveat_mode: Methodology explains corpus filters, tf-idf modifications, similarity, dimensionality reduction, and known interpretation limits.
stories.editorial_lesson: Advanced methods feel earned when the reader reaches them by following the author's curiosity rather than being handed an algorithm first.
stories.anti_copy_note: Learn the concrete-example-to-method ladder; never treat t-SNE or an artist map as a generic Pudding visual signature.

stories.title: What city is the microbrew capital of the US?
stories.question: What would ‘best beer city’ mean if quality and abundance have to be combined?
stories.argument_pattern: Publish one defensible weighting, then expose the subjectivity by allowing readers to change the assumptions and watch rankings move.
stories.human_angle: The project starts from a recurring social argument—everyone claims their city is best—and admits that the author's own definition is only one opinion.
stories.visual_necessity: The ranking is not a single fact; interactive movement shows sensitivity to weights and thresholds, making methodological subjectivity visible.
stories.design_move: Turn uncertainty about the scoring model into the main interaction instead of burying it in methodology.
stories.caveat_mode: Criteria restrictions and the arbitrariness of ‘best’ are acknowledged in both interface and methods.
stories.editorial_lesson: When a result depends on value judgments, reader-controlled weights can be an epistemic device rather than a dashboard feature.
stories.anti_copy_note: Reuse the idea of exposing assumptions; do not copy the weighted-pivot chart as a house style.

stories.title: The Unlikely Odds of Making it Big
stories.question: What do years of live-show histories reveal about how rare musical breakout success is?
stories.argument_pattern: Open with a recognizable success trajectory, contrast it with a slower path, then reveal the much larger population that never reaches the same milestone.
stories.human_angle: The story converts an abstract success rate into the careers of bands whose paths have recognizable hopes, stalls, and breakthroughs.
stories.visual_necessity: Career trajectories are sequences through time and venue scale; paths and search make the contrast between exceptional and typical careers visible.
stories.design_move: Teach the trajectory with a few named bands before handing the same representation to readers for lookup.
stories.caveat_mode: Venue capacity is explicitly framed as a proxy for success, with thresholds described as manual choices.
stories.editorial_lesson: A memorable individual example can teach the visual grammar before a population distribution delivers the actual argument.
stories.anti_copy_note: Learn the exemplar-to-population handoff, not the band's path styling or success thresholds.

stories.title: The Birthday Paradox Experiment
stories.question: Can a counterintuitive probability become intuitive if readers guess first and contribute their own birthdays?
stories.argument_pattern: Capture the reader's prior belief, demonstrate the mechanism, then compare personal intuition with a growing pool of reader responses.
stories.human_angle: The reader is not a spectator; their own guess and birthday become part of the explanation and the evolving dataset.
stories.visual_necessity: The gap between intuition and probability is experiential, and the evolving distribution of guesses makes collective misunderstanding visible.
stories.design_move: Ask for a commitment before revealing the answer so the interaction creates a cognitive stake in the result.
stories.caveat_mode: The project distinguishes theoretical even-distribution math from the real birthday data collected from readers.
stories.editorial_lesson: Interaction can manufacture the before-and-after mental state that the story needs, not merely let the reader filter existing evidence.
stories.anti_copy_note: Reuse the pre-commitment principle only when the reader's prior belief is central to the argument.

stories.title: Oreos and the Art of Crossword Puzzle Construction
stories.question: Why are certain odd words and clues so persistent in crossword construction?
stories.argument_pattern: Use a tiny absurd clue as an entry point, answer it quickly, then reward continued curiosity with deeper optional layers and playful side quests.
stories.human_angle: The story treats niche obsession itself as legitimate motivation and turns the author's rabbit hole into a reader-controlled depth choice.
stories.visual_necessity: Frequency, repetition, and word-pattern constraints are easier to see through compact visual counts and interactive word play than through exposition alone.
stories.design_move: Offer multiple reading levels so a three-minute answer and a deep nerdy exploration can coexist without forcing every reader through the same length.
stories.caveat_mode: Database scope and historical frequency are kept distinct from claims about editorial intent.
stories.editorial_lesson: Delight can come from respecting a weird obsession and designing pacing around optional depth instead of inflating a small finding into a grand thesis.
stories.anti_copy_note: Learn progressive disclosure and tonal permission; do not copy the level system or jokes.

stories.title: How Bad Is Your Streaming Music?
stories.question: What if a reader's own listening history became the raw material for a satirical cultural critique?
stories.argument_pattern: Replace a general essay about taste with a personalized adversarial conversation built from the reader's actual music metadata and a curated joke system.
stories.human_angle: The reader's identity and taste are the content, creating emotional stakes through teasing, recognition, and self-reflection.
stories.visual_necessity: The essential medium is interactive personalization rather than a chart; a static article cannot reproduce the same individualized sequence.
stories.design_move: Treat interface, timing, and voice as the visual essay rather than forcing conventional charts into a product-like experience.
stories.caveat_mode: Privacy and data access behavior are disclosed, including the limits of the faux-AI framing.
stories.editorial_lesson: A Pudding-like story can be a data-driven experience with almost no traditional chart grammar if personalization is the argument-bearing mechanism.
stories.anti_copy_note: Learn that format follows the idea; do not reproduce the faux-snob voice, joke bank, or branded interaction.

stories.title: How many days since a record-high temperature?
stories.question: How can the growing frequency of extreme heat be made locally and temporally tangible?
stories.argument_pattern: Translate climate trend data into a continuously updating local recency measure that makes record heat feel immediate rather than abstract.
stories.human_angle: Readers can connect a global phenomenon to familiar cities and recent days instead of only seeing century-scale averages.
stories.visual_necessity: Map position and recency encode where records are happening and how recently, letting a living pattern emerge at a glance.
stories.design_move: Choose a metric whose meaning updates naturally over time so the page remains a living instrument rather than a frozen article.
stories.caveat_mode: Station threading, relocation, and long-series construction are documented in the data notes.
stories.editorial_lesson: Timeliness can be encoded into the metric itself, but only if the underlying data pipeline and methodology remain legible.
stories.anti_copy_note: Learn the living-metric idea; do not treat map recency as a generic climate template.

stories.title: Flooding in America
stories.question: Where do two systems for estimating flood risk materially disagree?
stories.argument_pattern: Put competing risk models into the same geographic frame, quantify their disagreement, then let communities inspect local consequences.
stories.human_angle: Differences between models matter because they can change how residents understand property risk and insurance-relevant exposure.
stories.visual_necessity: Geographic disagreement is inherently spatial, and maps plus local tables show both pattern and consequence.
stories.design_move: Keep the comparison frame stable while switching model views so disagreement is the visual subject.
stories.caveat_mode: The page identifies each model's role and frames one dataset as an additional perspective rather than a universal replacement.
stories.editorial_lesson: When two authoritative-looking estimates conflict, visualize the disagreement itself instead of silently choosing one source.
stories.anti_copy_note: Learn paired-model comparison; do not reuse map assets, tiles, or geographic styling.

stories.title: Using an A.I. program to win the New Yorker cartoon caption contest
stories.question: Can a human-machine feedback process improve joke writing enough to compete in a real caption contest?
stories.argument_pattern: Treat a provocative technology claim as an experiment, expose iteration and failure, and keep human judgment inside the system rather than presenting automation as magic.
stories.human_angle: Humor creates an immediate human standard: outputs can be technically plausible yet still fail because people simply do not laugh.
stories.visual_necessity: The project benefits from showing iterations, choices, and examples as a process; the interface documents collaboration rather than only reporting a final score.
stories.design_move: Make the feedback loop and imperfect intermediate outputs part of the story rather than hiding them behind a polished final result.
stories.caveat_mode: Human involvement and the limits of computational humor are foregrounded rather than treated as implementation details.
stories.editorial_lesson: Process can be the evidence when the question is about whether a new creative workflow actually works.
stories.anti_copy_note: Learn the experiment-as-story frame; do not reproduce their prompts, cartoons, model outputs, or comedic voice.

stories.title: Outkast, in Charts
stories.question: What does Outkast’s history look like when lyrical themes, language, collaborators, and life events are treated as evidence?
stories.argument_pattern: Build a portrait of one cultural subject through a sequence of focused charts and reported context rather than through one master interactive.
stories.human_angle: The author’s fandom and curiosity about hip-hop history are explicit, so the charts answer specific questions about an artist rather than decorating a retrospective.
stories.visual_necessity: Multiple small, mostly static charts let different kinds of evidence—language, themes, geography, collaborators, and chronology—sit beside reported context without forcing one interaction model.
stories.design_move: Use a sequence of self-contained visuals, each paired with editorial interpretation, so the story can change visual form when the evidence changes.
stories.caveat_mode: The piece distinguishes quantitative counts from interpretive cultural history and uses reported context where data alone cannot establish meaning.
stories.editorial_lesson: Static charts are a first-class visual-story form: if each chart advances a distinct part of the argument, interactivity is optional rather than a marker of ambition.
stories.anti_copy_note: Learn the chart-sequence discipline; do not copy the typography, chart styling, artist framing, or specific Outkast analysis.
